newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia end-March palm oil stock seen at 605,000t.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia end-March palm oil stock seen at 605,000t.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil stocks are expected to fall to 605,000 tonnes at end-March 1997 from an estimated 850,000 tonnes at end-December 1996, the U.S. embassy said on Friday.
It said stocks were at 699,000 tonnes at end-March 1996.

"With lower domestic crude palm oil output anticipated during the January-March period, palm oil stocks level is expected to drop around 600,000 tonnes at the end of March 1997," it said in a report prepared by the U.S. agricultural attache in Kuala Lumpur.

The embassy said output in January/November 1996 totalled 7.74 million tonnes versus 7.16 million tonnes in the same period of 1995. Production in December is expected to fall 15-20 percent from November, it said.
"The drop in output signalled the beginning of the normal seasonal downtrend in output," the embassy added.
Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority said output in November fell 14 percent to 762,540 tonnes.
The embassy said the outlook of lower output and stock levels in the coming months pushed up palm oil prices during the second half of December.
"The average monthly crude palm oil price for December was 1,230 ringgit a tonne against 1,184 in November," it said.
